az_3_south_end.blurb: South End is the southern half of a volcanic cliff high on the flank of the San Francisco Peaks above Flagstaff, at roughly 8,700 feet. Most of the 26 climbs here are bolted, with a handful of trad lines, and the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.12, with a few harder and only a couple of easy options. Expect steep, sustained pulling on weathered dacite, with a boulder-strewn base and views toward town. The face gets strong morning sun and is shaded by early afternoon, so it suits warm days. The access road is shut by snow in winter.

az_beer_bong_boulder.blurb: Beer Bong Boulder is one block within the Icecapades bouldering zone north of Phoenix, tucked low on the east side of a small cove. The 26 problems are thin and vertical to slightly overhanging on sharp granite-type rock, and the north-facing lines stay a bit cooler than much of the valley. Most are in the V0 to V4 range, with a few much harder outliers up near V7 to V9. Rock quality varies and some of it is crumbly, and the landings call for pads.

az_donkey_punch_area.blurb: Donkey Punch Area is the busiest cluster of problems in East Kelly Canyon, a bouldering canyon a few miles south of Flagstaff reached by Kelly Canyon Road off I-17. The sandstone here is slopey and gymnastic, and many problems finish on tall, demanding topouts, so bring extra pads and spotters. Our 26 problems run from about V1 to V9, with a good middle weight of V3 to V6 and a few hard test pieces. The rock is fragile when wet: skip it for at least a day after rain and avoid anything damp or seeping. Road access to the upper canyon has changed over the years, so check before going.

az_redbud_canyon.blurb: Redbud Canyon is a side canyon at the back of Lime Kiln Canyon, just across the Nevada line from Mesquite. It holds 26 sport routes, mostly single pitch with a couple of longer ones, from about 5.7 to 5.12 and clustered in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. The grey limestone is vertical to slabby, with runnels and pockets, and the canyon is shady and noticeably cooler than town. Plan on a walk of 5 to 10 minutes beyond the main walls after a roughly 20 minute uphill hike from the trailhead. Some rock is loose, so wear helmets. The long dirt road in suits spring and fall.

az_old_tunnel_area.blurb: Old Tunnel Area is a short sport crag in Queen Creek Canyon, about an hour east of Phoenix, found along an abandoned stretch of the old highway that runs through a former tunnel. Nearly all of our 26 climbs are bolted, with two trad lines, ranging from beginner-friendly to low 5.12 and bunching around 5.10. The rock is volcanic tuff with reasonable quality, and the sun arrives mid-morning and warms it fast, making this a good winter stop. It is a few minutes from the car.

az_lower_pumphouse_wash.blurb: Lower Pumphouse Wash is a small collection of short crags along a creek bed that drains into Oak Creek Canyon, between Flagstaff and Sedona. The 26 routes are a mix of newer sport lines and some trad on sandstone that ranges from very good to poor. Most grades fall from 5.10 to 5.11, with a handful of moderates and a couple at 5.12. The canyon is shady, so it makes a cool alternative when Sedona heats up. The approach follows the streambed for 5 to 10 minutes, and depending on water levels and your height you may wade or swim. Roadside parking at the bottom of the switchbacks is limited.

az_beaver_wall.blurb: Beaver Wall is a broad, orange, slightly overhanging cliff just southwest of the Windy Point viewpoint on Mount Lemmon above Tucson, at around 6,500 feet. It is mainly a hard sport wall: of our 26 climbs, most sit between 5.12 and 5.14, with only a few moderates, mostly trad, near the south end. Parking is at the Windy Point lot; the walk is about five minutes along the ridge trail and then down a steep path. The face points east and south, so it catches morning light. Expect cool, crisp conditions to be best for the technical, fingery climbing.
